title: I Took the Boxing-Ring Round Timer to the Coach Who Ran an Extra

parts.text: I stepped in at 6:31 p.m. and coach Iker let the bell run a fourth on a three-round card. The card said: THREE ROUNDS. BELL ENDS. NO EXTRA. I was twenty-five, amateur, holding a round card. Iker shrugged. "Coaches are the bell." I photographed the card, the clock, and the fourth light. Then I asked for the round log. At 6:37 the gym manager pinged why Iker's name was on an extra round. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The gym manager can see Iker's fourth light on a three-round card.

social.video_title: The coach ran a fourth round on a three-round card — Part 1/2
social.description: Boxing gym, a round card, a bell that kept going. I logged the extra. Would you have asked the manager?

parts.text: Iker called it grit until the manager asked for the still. I printed the log, the card, and the photo. The bell ended on three. Iker ran cards as written and told the next coach grit was always about optics. Optics is a word coaches use when bells exist. Timer policy now has a second line: COACHES ARE NOT THE BELL. I keep three. Iker brown-bags the jokes. The ring finally looks like a card, not a dare. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches are not the bell — Part 2/2
social.description: Round log, three bells, and a second line. Was grit ever a fourth?
